capabilities: Run agent tasks such as refactoring, link auditing, frontmatter cleanup, and MOC generation from the command palette
Embed the Antigravity web hub UI in an Obsidian tab
Inject an AGENTS.md rules file so the agent follows vault conventions like wikilinks and YAML frontmatter
Pass the active note, selection, or folder as context to the agent automatically
Cancel running agent tasks via the status bar indicator
extras: Not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Reads ~/.gemini/ OAuth credentials to bootstrap the hub without a second login. Unrestricted autonomous execution (--dangerously-skip-permissions) is gated behind a setting, per-path confirmations, and a persistent risk banner. Desktop only.
intentEvidence: It builds on Antigravity's agentic filesystem access instead of a multi-provider chat framework.
motivation: The README says it deliberately avoids wrapping Antigravity in a chat interface, offering discrete tasks and an optional embedded hub instead.
problem: Using agentic AI on a vault normally means a chat-style plugin; there was no way to run an agent as discrete vault-maintenance commands with permission gating.

relations.evidence: connects your vault to Google Antigravity's agy CLI, letting an agent read, reorganize, and maintain your notes

summary: AI agent bridge that runs Google Antigravity's agy CLI to reorganize, audit, and maintain vault notes through discrete tasks and an embedded web hub.
